title.en: The price puzzle: demand, supply and market equilibrium
Why mangoes cost more in winter

text.en: Mangoes are cheap in summer and costly out of season. Prices are not random; they depend on how much people want and how much is available.

Demand is the quantity of a good that buyers are willing and able to buy at a price. When price rises, demand usually falls.
Supply is the quantity sellers offer at a price. When price rises, supply usually rises.
Factors like income, tastes, prices of related goods and expectations shift demand; costs and technology shift supply.
The market equilibrium price is where the quantity demanded equals the quantity supplied.
If price is above equilibrium there is a surplus, and sellers cut the price. If it is below, there is a shortage and the price rises.
Real markets seldom stay exactly at equilibrium but keep moving towards it.
Governments sometimes intervene with a price ceiling, such as a maximum price, or a price floor like the minimum support price for crops.
Such rules protect consumers or producers but can cause shortages or surpluses.

text.en: Demand exceeds supply: a shortage of 40.
